theorems.name: Kelly Numéraire Deflator Makes the Bet Fair (Discrete, Two-Outcome)
theorems.description: In the two-outcome bet (win probability 0 < p < 1, odds b > 0), deflate the physical probabilities by the growth-optimal (Kelly) terminal wealth W*₊ = 1 + f*·b, W*₋ = 1 − f*, where f* = (p·b − (1 − p))/b is the Kelly fraction. theorems.description: If μ_post solves the Black–Litterman normal equation (Σ⁻¹ + PᵀΩ⁻¹P) μ_post = Σ⁻¹π + PᵀΩ⁻¹Q and the precisions Σ⁻¹, Ω⁻¹ are positive semidefinite, then μ_post minimises the Theil–Goldberger mixed-estimation loss ½(μ − π)ᵀΣ⁻¹(μ − π) + ½(Pμ − Q)ᵀΩ⁻¹(Pμ − Q). The normal equation is taken as the definition of the posterior mean; its derivation by Gaussian conditioning is not formalized.

import MathFin.Portfolio.BlackLittermanND

open MathFin

/-- **The Black–Litterman posterior mean is a generalized-least-squares minimiser.** -/
theorem black_litterman_gls_minimizer_thm {n m : ℕ} {μ_post π : Fin n → ℝ} {Q : Fin m → ℝ}
    {Sg_inv : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {P : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ}
    {Om_inv : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} (h : IsBLPosteriorMean μ_post π Q Sg_inv P Om_inv)
    (hS : Sg_inv.PosSemidef) (hO : Om_inv.PosSemidef) (μ : Fin n → ℝ) :
    blLoss π Q Sg_inv P Om_inv μ_post ≤ blLoss π Q Sg_inv P Om_inv μ :=
  h.blLoss_le hS hO μ

theorems.name: Single-Index Model: Portfolio Variance from the Return Model
theorems.description: For returns Rᵢ = βᵢ R_M + εᵢ with square-integrable market return R_M and shocks εᵢ, the shocks uncorrelated with the market and with each other, and Var[R_M] = σ_M², the portfolio return has Var[∑ wᵢ Rᵢ] = (∑ wᵢβᵢ)² σ_M² + ∑ wᵢ² Var[εᵢ]: the single-index covariance kernel is derived from the return model.

import MathFin.Portfolio.SingleIndexModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- **Single-index portfolio variance from the return model.** -/
theorem single_index_variance_from_returns_thm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι)
    (w β : ι → ℝ) (σM : ℝ) {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure P] {RM : Ω → ℝ} {ε : ι → Ω → ℝ} (hRM : MemLp RM 2 P)
    (hε : ∀ i, MemLp (ε i) 2 P) (hRMε : ∀ i, cov[RM, ε i; P] = 0)
    (hεε : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → cov[ε i, ε j; P] = 0) (hσM : Var[RM; P] = σM ^ 2) :
    Var[∑ i ∈ s, w i • (β i • RM + ε i); P] =
      (∑ i ∈ s, w i * β i) ^ 2 * σM ^ 2 + ∑ i ∈ s, w i ^ 2 * Var[ε i; P] :=
  MathFin.variance_singleIndex_portfolio s w β σM hRM hε hRMε hεε hσM

theorems.name: Single-Index Loading Is the CAPM Beta
theorems.description: For returns Rᵢ = βᵢ R_M + εᵢ with square-integrable R_M and εᵢ, shocks uncorrelated with the market and Var[R_M] ≠ 0, the CAPM beta cov(Rᵢ, R_M)/Var[R_M] of asset i equals its loading βᵢ.

theorems.name: Sigmoid Bet Size of the Probability z-Score Is the Even-Money Kelly Fraction
theorems.description: For a predicted win probability 0 < p < 1 with z-statistic z = (p − ½)/√(p(1 − p)) and any width w > 0, López de Prado's sigmoid bet size m(x) = x/√(w + x²) at x = √w·z equals 2p − 1, the Kelly fraction (p·b − (1 − p))/b of an even-money bet (b = 1). López de Prado's probability-based size 2Φ(z) − 1 is a different map and is not covered.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Performance.BetSizeSigmoid

/-- **The sigmoid of the probability z-score is the even-money Kelly fraction.** -/
theorem bet_size_sigmoid_zscore_kelly_thm {w p : ℝ} (hw : 0 < w) (hp₀ : 0 < p)
    (hp₁ : p < 1) :
    betSize w (√w * ((p - 1 / 2) / √(p * (1 - p)))) = kellyFraction p 1 :=
  MathFin.betSize_sqrt_mul_zScore hw hp₀ hp₁

theorems.name: Fractional-Differencing Weights Are the Binomial Series of (1 − x)^d

theorems.name: First-Difference Drift Estimator of Brownian Motion with Drift Has Law N(μ, σ²/T)
theorems.description: Let X_t = μt + σB_t with B a pre-Brownian motion, observed at the n ≥ 1 equally spaced times kT/n of [0, T]. The drift estimator (1/T)∑ᵢ (Δ¹X)ᵢ₊₁, built from the d = 1 fractionally differenced observations, has law N(μ, σ²/T) for every n: it telescopes to (X_T − X_0)/T, so sampling more often does not reduce the standard error σ/√T. Only the case d = 1 (the first difference) of fractional differencing is involved.

open scoped NNReal

theorem drift_estimator_differenced_law_thm {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {P : Measure Ω} {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B P) (mu sigma : ℝ)
    {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :

  MathFin.hasLaw_fracDiff_one_driftEstimator hB mu sigma hT hn

theorems.name: Purged Cross-Validation: Surviving Training Labels Are Independent of Test Labels
theorems.description: Let every label be a measurable function of the increments of a pre-Brownian motion over its own nonempty span [lo, hi] ⊆ [0, ∞). If a training label survives purging (its span neither starts inside, ends inside nor envelops any test span), then it is independent of every test label. Pairwise only: joint independence of the whole test fold from the whole surviving training set, embargoing, and labels with random spans are not covered.
